title: Low Tide: Seven Samples
statement: Mara cut the beach open and showed seven tides filed in the sand. I took one from each. A core tube goes down through the section at the right of centre, pale against the strata, and beside the face stand seven small stoppered vials in a column, one for each layer, the weed in each a little paler and more broken the deeper it came from, with a tally of red strokes on every vial counting its depth and a dashed stamp at the foot of the column. The section is still open; the vials are what leaves with me. A tide a month old is a smell; a tide seven months old is a sample. The next hand can put the samples back in their layers, or take the eighth from below the picture.
process: I kept Mara's section exactly, the surface, grass, roots and seven buried strata with their bladders, and added a pale core tube cut vertically through all seven layers, a column of seven labelled vials at the right each holding a sample from its layer with a tally of depth marks, a vertical guide line and a stamp circle.
